_comment: The canonical admin URL per Instatic site — the single answer to 'what link do I send?'.
`adminUrl` is the origin a person should work from; `check-origins.mjs` appends its www/apex
twin automatically, so list only what that would not derive: a second client domain, the
platform host, staging, an old domain people still have bookmarked.
List a host even when it is currently broken — a host nobody checks is a host nobody fixes,
and the checker's job is to keep saying so until it is clean.
This file is the claim; `node check-origins.mjs --all` is the proof, and it probes the RUNNING
server rather than the Railway dashboard. Re-run it after any domain change or redeploy and
fix whichever of the two is wrong.
No secrets here. Credentials live in the per-worktree .env and never in this repo.

sites.note: Fixed 2026-08-28: www.drnahlah.com and drnahlah.com appended to PUBLIC_ORIGIN, which already held encorercm.com + www + the railway host from the 2026-08-18 fix. drnahlah.com 301s to www, so www is the one that must be listed. All five origins verified live.

Fixed 2026-08-28. PUBLIC_ORIGIN had been set to the apex alone (https://masonparkdental.com) and had NEVER been applied — the container was still running its boot-time derived value. The apex also has no DNS record, so it is listed for the day it gets one but is not the link to hand out. Redeployed; www now verified live. 2026-08-31: mason-park.up.railway.app now answers 404 'Application not found' — the service domain was removed, so the Railway host is dead while the custom domain is healthy. It stays listed because PUBLIC_ORIGIN still names it and the checker should keep saying so until one of the two is corrected.

Added 2026-08-31, the day the rebuilt site was imported (54 pages). The service domain was generated from the IMAGE name (corebunchinstaticlatest-production-fb3b) and was renamed the same day to match the convention the other two sites use. Renaming a service domain silently invalidates PUBLIC_ORIGIN, which is the 403-on-login trap this module exists for, so the order was: widen PUBLIC_ORIGIN to hold BOTH hosts, confirm the container had actually applied it, rename, then narrow it back to the new host alone. pediatricdentistkatytx.com is still on SiteGround DNS and 301s to the parent practice's now-dead mason-park.up.railway.app; when it moves to Cloudflare and points here, add apex AND www to PUBLIC_ORIGIN and re-run the checker BEFORE sending anyone the link. 2026-09-14: the site's domain became masonparkpediatricdental.com (Squarespace registrar, Cloudflare DNS). Apex and www added in Railway, PUBLIC_ORIGIN = www, apex, railway host; redeployed; all three verified OK live.
